title: Alcimus urges Demetrius to act against Judas for the country’s sake
speaker: Alcimus, the former high priest
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Parallel account of Alcimus’s appeal to Demetrius (1 Maccabees 7:5–7); link 2 Maccabees 14:9–10 as Additional Scripture.

title: Demetrius appoints Nicanor governor of Judea with orders to kill Judas
speaker: King Demetrius
recipient: Nicanor, former commander of the elephants
note: Also ordered to scatter Judas’s men and install Alcimus as high priest. The parallel 1 Maccabees 7:26 is not itemized either.

title: Nicanor sends envoys to give and receive pledges with Judas
speaker: Nicanor
note: Envoys sent with a charge, like the catalogue’s messenger commissions (e.g. Esther 4:10).

title: Nicanor urges Judas to marry and have children
speaker: Nicanor
note: Reported urging; Judas complies, marries and settles down.

title: Demetrius orders Nicanor to send Judas in chains to Antioch
speaker: King Demetrius, by letter
note: Outside candidate list: royal written order prompted by Alcimus’s slander (14:26); Nicanor receives ‘these instructions’ (14:28).

title: Nicanor orders the priests to hand over Judas, threatening the temple
speaker: Nicanor
recipient: the priests offering sacrifice in the temple
note: Sworn threat to level the sanctuary and build a temple to Dionysus. Parallel 1 Maccabees 7:33–35 is not itemized.

title: Nicanor sends five hundred soldiers to arrest Razis
speaker: Nicanor
note: Outside candidate list (candidate 14:42 is narrative). Reported sending with orders to arrest, like AUD-16-5-11.

title: Jewish companions urge Nicanor to honor the Sabbath God commanded
speaker: the Jews compelled to accompany Nicanor
note: Adds 15:3–4: asked who commanded it, they reply that the living Lord in heaven commanded the seventh day be observed.

title: Nicanor commands arms taken up on the Sabbath for the king’s business
speaker: Nicanor
recipient: his army, including the Jews compelled to accompany him
note: His counter-claim to command as ‘sovereign on earth’, answering 15:4; the narrator says he did not succeed.

title: Judas orders Nicanor’s head and hand displayed and his tongue cut up
speaker: Judas Maccabeus
recipient: his men and the people gathered at Jerusalem
note: 15:30 (outside candidate list) begins the orders; 15:33 has the tongue given to birds. Cf. 1 Maccabees 7:47, not itemized.

title: Wine mixed with water delights, as a well-ordered account does
speaker: the epitomist (author of 2 Maccabees)
note: Epilogue maxim that unmixed wine or water harms; a borderline literary analogy, so low.

title: The governor bars unproven priests from eating the most holy things
speaker: Athersatha (the governor)
recipient: priestly families unable to prove their descent
note: Until a priest arises with the illuminating and perfect things (Urim and Thummim). Same ruling at Nehemiah 7:65 (P01208).

title: Officials urge Artaxerxes to search the records and halt Jerusalem’s rebuilding
speaker: Raoum the baaltam, Samsai the scribe and their colleagues
note: Petition by letter; compare the catalogue’s record of an opponent’s appeal to a king (ot-1-maccabees-v7-7).

title: The king orders the rebuilding stopped and warns against slackness
speaker: Arthasastha (Artaxerxes) the king
note: Adds 4:22, the same decree’s charge: be on guard against slackness lest harm increase to kings.

title: Thanthanai asks Darius to search the archives for Cyrus’s decree
speaker: Thanthanai the governor, Satharbouzana and their colleagues
note: Petition by letter; also asks the king to send word of his decision.

title: Darius orders a search of the royal archives in Babylon
speaker: Darius the king
note: Outside candidate list: the king’s decision answering 5:17; it leads to Cyrus’s archived decree (6:3).

title: Darius orders officials to keep away from the work and fund it
speaker: Darius the king
recipient: Thanthanai, Satharbouzana and the officials beyond the river
note: Adds 6:6, the opening of the same order (‘keeping far away from there’).

title: Ezra sends leaders to bring Levites and temple servants for God’s house
speaker: Ezra
recipient: Eleazar, Ariel, Samaia and other leading men
note: Outside candidate list: finding no Levites (8:15), Ezra sends men with words to speak, to bring ministers.

title: Ezra proclaims a fast at the river to seek a safe journey
speaker: Ezra

title: God’s hand is good to those who seek him, wrath on deserters
speaker: Ezra, recalling his words to the king
note: Same principle as 2 Chronicles 15:2 in AUD-14-15-1 (seek him and he is found; forsake him and he forsakes you).

title: Ezra sets apart twelve priests to carry and guard the holy gifts
speaker: Ezra
note: Adds 8:24–28: Ezra sets apart the twelve, weighs the offerings into their hands and declares them and the vessels holy.

title: Ezra makes the leaders and all Israel swear to the proposal
speaker: Ezra
recipient: the leaders, priests, Levites and all Israel
note: Outside candidate list: the oath executing Shecaniah’s covenant proposal (10:3); compare Nehemiah 5:12 (Instruction).

title: Ezra and family heads are set apart to examine the foreign marriages
speaker: the returned community
recipient: Ezra the priest and the heads of ancestral houses
note: Carries out the hearing plan of 10:14 (ot-ezra-v10-14) by appointing the examiners.

title: If Israel returns and keeps God’s commandments, he will regather them
speaker: Nehemiah, quoting the Lord’s word to Moses
note: The prayer quotes Deuteronomy 30:1–4 (cf. Leviticus 26:33); link as Additional Scripture, as the recalled law at Ezra 9:12 was recorded.

title: Artaxerxes sends Nehemiah to Judah to rebuild Jerusalem
speaker: Arthasastha (Artaxerxes) the king, at Nehemiah’s request
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Outside candidate list (2:6 is a context verse): Nehemiah’s request (2:5) and the king’s sending with a time limit (2:6).

title: Nehemiah asks the king for letters of passage and timber
speaker: Nehemiah
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Letters to the governors beyond the river and to Asaph, keeper of the king’s park; the king grants them.

title: Nehemiah’s enemies plot a surprise attack to stop the work
speaker: Sanaballat, Tobia and the other adversaries
note: A plot, recorded as the catalogue records plots at Genesis 37:20 and Exodus 1:10 (Instruction).

title: Nehemiah orders the builders to rally wherever the horn sounds
speaker: Nehemiah
recipient: the nobles, leaders and people building the wall
note: Outside candidate list; the chapter’s records cover only 4:8 and 4:16.

title: Nehemiah has the lenders swear and seals the oath with a curse
speaker: Nehemiah
recipient: the priests, the lenders and the assembly
note: Adds 5:13: he shakes out his garment against oath-breakers; the assembly says Amen and carries out the word.

title: The governor bars unproven priests from eating the most holy things
speaker: Athersatha (the governor)
recipient: priestly families unable to prove their descent
note: Same ruling as Ezra 2:63 (P01186 finding): make one record and add this verse as Additional Scripture.

title: The people ask Ezra to bring the book of Moses’ law
speaker: all the people gathered at the Water Gate
note: Ezra brings the law and reads it to the assembly (8:2–3).

title: God told Israel to enter and possess the promised land
speaker: Ezra (Esdras) in prayer, recalling the Lord’s command
note: Recollection in prayer of the command to go in and inherit the land (Deuteronomy 1:8, 21).

title: Whoever does God’s judgments will live by them
speaker: Ezra (Esdras) in prayer, recalling the law
topic: Marriage, family and care for parents
note: Echoes Leviticus 18:5 within the prayer’s confession; link as Additional Scripture.

title: The Levites are summoned to Jerusalem for the wall’s dedication
speaker: the leaders at Jerusalem
note: Brought to celebrate with thanksgivings, songs, cymbals, psalteries and lyres.

title: Nehemiah stations two great thanksgiving choirs on the wall
speaker: Nehemiah
recipient: the rulers of Judah and two companies of singers
note: Outside candidate list; the dedication rite of 12:27–43 has no record.

title: The people cast lots to settle one in ten in Jerusalem
speaker: the people and their rulers
recipient: the families of Judah outside Jerusalem
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Outside candidate list (no passage in chapter 11): a communal resettlement decision by lot.

title: Nehemiah warns Sabbath traders and shuts the gates against Sabbath trade
speaker: Nehemiah
recipient: those trading on the Sabbath, the nobles of Judah and his servants
note: Adds 13:15–18: he warns those selling on the Sabbath and rebukes Judah’s nobles for profaning it.

title: Ammonites and Moabites must not enter God’s assembly
speaker: the book of Moses, read to the people
note: Outside candidate list: public reading of Deuteronomy 23:4–5; 13:3 records the separation that followed.

title: Nehemiah charges the Levites to guard the gates and hallow the Sabbath
speaker: Nehemiah
note: The prayer in the rest of the verse is out of scope.

title: Nehemiah sets duty divisions for priests and Levites and the wood offering
speaker: Nehemiah
recipient: the priests, Levites and wood carriers
note: Includes the firstfruits (bakchouria); the prayers in 13:29 and 13:31 are out of scope.

title: The king orders the stewards to follow his and the guests’ wishes
speaker: King Artaxerxes
recipient: the stewards of the royal household
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Reported order governing the drinking at the feast.

title: The king orders the eunuchs to bring Queen Astin before him
speaker: King Artaxerxes
note: Outside candidate list: the order Astin refuses (1:12), which 1:15 calls ‘what the king commanded through the eunuchs’.

title: The king publishes the decree so that wives honor their husbands
speaker: King Artaxerxes, adopting Muchaeus’s proposal
note: Outside candidate list: adds 1:21–22, where the king enacts the proposal and sends it to each territory in its own language.

title: The proposal to gather young women and make the favored one queen
speaker: the king’s attendants
note: Adds 2:4, the same proposal’s last clause: the woman who pleases the king shall reign in Astin’s place.

title: Mordecai commands Esther not to reveal her ancestry or homeland
speaker: Mordecai
note: Repeated at 2:20; link that verse here too.

title: Mordecai instructs Esther to fear God and keep his commandments
speaker: Mordecai
note: Greek text; the verse also restates the non-disclosure order of 2:10.

title: The king orders Mordecai’s loyalty recorded in the royal library
speaker: King Artaxerxes
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Outside candidate list: the commendation later read to the king (6:1–2).

title: The king commands everyone at court to bow down before Haman
speaker: King Artaxerxes
note: 3:3–4: the courtiers press Mordecai daily to obey the king’s word; he refuses.

title: Haman asks the king to decree the destruction of the Jews
speaker: Haman
note: Accuses the Jews of disobeying the king’s laws and offers ten thousand talents; leads to 3:10–11 (ot-esther-v3-11).

title: Esther sends Achrathaeus to learn from Mordecai what has happened
speaker: Queen Esther
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Like the catalogue’s 4:10 messenger record (ot-esther-v4-10); 4:4 reports her earlier sending of clothes.

title: Esther invites the king and Haman to her reception
speaker: Queen Esther
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: A request to the king, answering his offer in 5:3.

title: The king orders Haman brought quickly to Esther’s reception
speaker: King Artaxerxes
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Compare the catalogue’s summons record at 6:5 (ot-esther-v6-5).

title: Esther asks the king and Haman to come again tomorrow
speaker: Queen Esther
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Her second invitation, made at the first drinking feast.

title: The sleepless king orders the chronicles brought and read to him
speaker: King Artaxerxes
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: The reading uncovers Mordecai’s unrewarded loyalty (6:2–3).

title: Esther pleads with the king for her life and her people
speaker: Queen Esther
note: Her decisive petition at the second feast; the king’s offer (7:2) is not itself a directive.

title: Esther asks the king to revoke Haman’s letters against the Jews
speaker: Queen Esther
note: 8:3 and 8:5 (context verses) carry the request; 8:6 is its plea. Leads to the counter-decree (ot-esther-v8-8).

title: The king grants a second day and orders Haman’s sons hanged
speaker: King Artaxerxes
note: Outside candidate list: the royal order granting Esther’s request (ot-esther-v9-13).

title: The days of Adar are to be kept through all generations
speaker: Mordecai
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Outside candidate list: Greek Addition F restates the perpetual observance of 14–15 Adar; link as Additional Scripture.

title: Job summons and purifies his children, offering sacrifices for them
speaker: Job
note: Job’s habitual practice: he sends for his children to be purified, lest they had cursed God in their hearts.

title: The Lord gave and the Lord took away; bless his name
speaker: Job
recipient: spoken in worship before the Lord
note: 1:21 is a context verse (outside candidate list): a maxim of acceptance; cf. Ecclesiastes 5:14 and 1 Timothy 6:7.

title: Job rebukes his wife: bear evil from God as well as good
speaker: Job
note: Answers his wife’s urging (ot-job-v2-9e); counsel to a person, not an appeal to God.

title: Eliphaz: those who plow wrong and sow it reap pains
speaker: Eliphaz the Temanite
note: Outside candidate list (follows the 4:7 Study Context record); the friends’ counsel, which God later faults (42:7); cf. Galatians 6:7.

title: Eliphaz: anger kills the fool, and his prosperity is soon devoured
speaker: Eliphaz the Temanite
note: Covers candidate 5:5 (P01251) as well; the friends’ counsel, recorded with its speaker.

title: God catches the wise in their own understanding
speaker: Eliphaz the Temanite
note: Quoted in 1 Corinthians 3:19 inside AUD-50-3-18; link as Additional Scripture (from Eliphaz’s doxology, 5:9–16).

title: Eliphaz urges Job to examine for himself whether he has sinned
speaker: Eliphaz the Temanite
note: Closing charge of Eliphaz’s first speech, after the promises of 5:18–26.

title: Those who trust in cities and possessions will be put to shame
speaker: Job
note: 6:20 (context verse) states the maxim within Job’s complaint about faithless friends.

title: Bildad urges Job to seek God and be pure and true
speaker: Bildad the Shuhite
note: Adds 8:6, the condition joined to the call: ‘If you are pure and true, He will hear your supplication.’

title: Bildad urges Job to learn from the former generations
speaker: Bildad the Shuhite
note: Adds 8:9–10: the reason (we are of yesterday) and the promise that the fathers will teach him.

title: Bildad: the hope of those who forget the Lord will perish
speaker: Bildad the Shuhite
note: Outside candidate list (8:11 is a context verse): the papyrus saying; 8:14–19 elaborate it.

title: Bildad: the ungodly are uprooted, but God will not reject the innocent
speaker: Bildad the Shuhite
note: Conclusion of the papyrus illustration (8:14–19) with the maxim of 8:20.

title: Zophar: the one who says much will hear an answer
speaker: Zophar the Minaean
note: Also contains the Greek beatitude ‘Blessed is the one born of woman who lives a short life’.

title: Zophar tells Job to stop talking and not claim to be pure
speaker: Zophar the Minaean
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Adds 11:4: ‘Do not say, I am pure in my works and blameless before Him.’

title: Zophar urges Job to purify his heart and put away lawlessness
speaker: Zophar the Minaean
note: The promises that follow (11:15–19) are not directives.

title: Eliphaz: a wise person does not argue with useless words
speaker: Eliphaz the Temanite
note: A rhetorical question carrying a maxim on speech; borderline.

title: Eliphaz calls Job to hear what the wise have handed down
speaker: Eliphaz the Temanite
note: Compare the catalogue’s ‘listen’ Commands at Job 13:17 and 34:16.

title: Bildad: such is the dwelling of those who do not know God
speaker: Bildad the Shuhite
note: Sums up Bildad’s description of the ungodly’s end (18:5–20).

title: Job tells his friends to stop tormenting him: the Lord struck him
speaker: Job
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Adds 19:2–4 and 19:6: ‘How long will you weary my soul?… Know, then, that the Lord is the One who disturbed me.’

title: Job pleads with his friends to have mercy on him
speaker: Job
note: Addressed to the friends, not to God.

title: Job warns his friends to beware, for wrath comes on the lawless
speaker: Job

title: Zophar: the joy of the ungodly is brief and ends in ruin
speaker: Zophar the Minaean
note: Outside candidate list: thesis of Zophar’s second speech (after candidate 20:2); 20:6–29 elaborate it.

title: Eliphaz urges Job to return to the Lord and heed his words
speaker: Eliphaz the Temanite
note: Adds 22:21 (‘become firm… your fruit will be among good things’) and 22:23 (‘turn back and humble yourself before the Lord’).

title: The silver the ungodly hoard will pass to the righteous
speaker: Job
note: Part of Job’s description of the ungodly’s portion (27:13–23).

title: Job covenants with his eyes not to gaze at a virgin
speaker: Job, in his oath of clearance
note: The oath (31:1–40) is itemized only at 31:13–15; 31:2–4 give the motive: God sees every step. Cf. K007 (Matthew 5:28).

title: Job disowns deceit, a straying heart and the taking of gifts
speaker: Job, in his oath of clearance
note: Outside candidate list; oath clause (gifts as bribes) with the self-imprecation of 31:8.

title: Job renounces adultery as a fire that destroys to the roots
speaker: Job, in his oath of clearance
note: The self-curse of candidate 31:10 frames the maxim of 31:11–12: defiling a neighbor’s wife is a consuming fire.

title: Job did not withhold help from the poor, widow, orphan or naked
speaker: Job, in his oath of clearance
note: Outside candidate list; oath clause on care for the needy, motivated by fear of the Lord (31:23).

title: Job renounces trust in gold and the worship of sun and moon
speaker: Job, in his oath of clearance
note: Oath clause; 31:28 calls such worship lying before the Lord Most High. Cf. C0981 (Deuteronomy 4:19).

title: Do not rejoice when an enemy falls
speaker: Job, in his oath of clearance
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Outside candidate list: Job’s oath that he did not rejoice at his enemies’ fall; link as Additional Scripture.

title: Job kept his door open and lodged every stranger
speaker: Job, in his oath of clearance
note: Outside candidate list; oath clause on hospitality.

title: Job did not hide his sin but confessed it before all
speaker: Job, in his oath of clearance
note: Outside candidate list; oath clause (31:34 is a context verse).

title: Job tore up debtors’ bonds, taking nothing from the debtor
speaker: Job, in his oath of clearance
note: Greek text of the oath: for fear of the Lord he returned written bonds and exacted nothing.

title: Job did not exploit the land or wrong its owners
speaker: Job, in his oath of clearance
topic: Land, harvests and provision for the poor
note: Outside candidate list; final oath clause, with nettles and brambles as self-imprecation.

title: Elihu asks to be heard, since age does not guarantee wisdom
speaker: Elihu son of Barachel
note: Adds 32:11–13: ‘Give ear to my words’, and his warning that they not say they have found wisdom.

title: Elihu refuses to show partiality or be overawed by anyone
speaker: Elihu son of Barachel
note: A personal resolve of impartiality; borderline.

title: Elihu: God inspects everyone and repays each as he acts
speaker: Elihu son of Barachel
note: 34:9 forbids saying there is no inspection; 34:11 states repayment by deeds (cf. Romans 2:6 in AUD-49-2-1).

title: Elihu calls for attention and to look at the righteous God
speaker: Elihu son of Barachel
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Adds 34:17: ‘Look at the One who hates lawless things and destroys the wicked.’

title: Elihu: God is beyond harm or gain from human sin or righteousness
speaker: Elihu son of Barachel
topic: Historical commissions, journeys and public life
note: Adds 35:6–8: your sin or righteousness affects only humans like you, not God.

title: Elihu: the Lord does not reject the innocent but upholds the righteous
speaker: Elihu son of Barachel

title: Elihu: those who listen and serve prosper; the disobedient perish
speaker: Elihu son of Barachel
note: 36:10 reports God telling them to turn from injustice; candidate 36:12 completes the two ways.

title: Elihu: the Almighty judges justly, so the wise in heart fear him
speaker: Elihu son of Barachel
note: 37:24 is a context verse; compare AUD-20-28-28.

title: God calls Job to prepare to answer his questions
speaker: the Lord, from the whirlwind
note: Adds 38:4 ‘Report to Me, if you understand’; later ‘tell Me’ challenges are Study Context (38:18), hence low.

title: God directs Job to look at the beast made beside him
speaker: the Lord, from the cloud
note: Behemoth: the ironic challenges of 40:10–13 are Study Context, but this is a plain call to consider God’s work.

title: The rebel kings resolve to throw off the Lord’s bonds
speaker: the kings and rulers of the earth
note: A plot quoted in the psalm, recorded as the catalogue records plots at Genesis 11:4 and 37:20 (Instruction).

summary: Ezra–Esther and 2 Maccabees 14–15 lack many royal orders, requests and commissions (Nehemiah’s commission, Esther’s petitions, Ezra’s oath, Nicanor’s orders), and Job lacks most of the friends’ and Elihu’s counsel and Job’s oath of clearance; prayers, laments and God’s rhetorical questions were left out.
